title: Correct billing for server-side prompt expansion and sampling debug outputs
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem statement:

Customers and internal audits have reported occasional small but consistent mismatches between reported billed token counts and the tokens we observe in customer-side checkpoints for requests that use two optional server-side features: prompt macro expansion (placeholder expansion performed by the platform before tokenization) and sampling debug outputs (when logprobs/alternative-tokens are returned or when the model is asked to stream n-best candidates). These mismatches surface most often for long prompts with repeated macros and for streamed partial responses where the server emits auxiliary probability frames.

Observed failure modes:
- Underbilling/overbilling: For some requests our usage ledger shows +5 to +200 billed input tokens relative to the customer-side expected length after macro expansion is applied on the client. Root cause is inconsistent canonicalization: we charge based on post-expansion tokenization, but some client-side SDKs measure on pre-expanded text leading to apparent discrepancies.
- Double-counting with caching: When prefix-caching is enabled and a request uses a macro that expands to the cached prefix, the billing pipeline sometimes attributes both the cache-hit prefix and the expanded prompt as billable (duplicate accounting).
- Streaming auxiliary frames: When debug/logprob streaming is enabled, we emit additional frames with token marginal data. These frames include token text stubs that were previously ignored by metering; after instrumentation changes they began to be tokenized and billed as output tokens in some code paths.
- Quota enforcement confusion: Rate-limiting and quota checks currently consider the "input_token_estimate" produced early in the request lifecycle. This estimate is based on pre-expanded input which results in under-enforcement for some heavy-expansion requests, allowing bursts beyond quota before final billable counts are computed.

Investigation summary (what we've done so far):
- Reproduced example with internal test harness: created prompt template "{{user_bio}} Hello" where user_bio is a 500-token expansion pulled from DB; observed ledger shows +500 billed tokens but client-side SDK measurement reporting 0 expanded tokens (they measured before expansion).
- End-to-end trace added to one customer sandbox showing path: API handler -> preprocessor (macro expansion) -> tokenizer -> prefix cache lookup -> runtime. Confirmed the tokenizer currently runs twice in some code paths (once for routing/quotas, once for billing).
- Identified three code locations that perform tokenization: request-estimator (fast path), billing-worker (canonicalizer), and streaming-serializer (where auxiliary frames were accidentally fed into tokenizer).
- Ran dataset of 50k requests with macros and logprobs enabled to quantify effect: 0.7% of requests had billing delta > 50 tokens; 0.04% > 1000 tokens.

Proposed design and trade-offs:
1) Single canonicalization point: add a canonical "post-expansion canonical_text" that is the single source for billing token counts and for quota enforcement decisions. This text should be recorded in the request trace and used by downstream systems (billing-worker, quota-enforcer, streaming-serializer).
2) Expansion attribution metadata: store two fields in the usage record (both strings): "original_length" and "expanded_length", plus a small human-readable list of expansion diffs for auditing (limited to 1KB). These fields allow transparent customer-facing reconciliation but keep the pipeline simple.
3) Cache dedup normalization: when prefix cache hits occur, billing should not double-count tokens if the cached prefix matches the canonical expanded prefix. Implement a dedupe step in billing that compares canonicalized token spans rather than naive concatenation lengths.
4) Streaming frame guardrails: ensure auxiliary frames (logprobs, marginal candidates) are explicitly marked as non-billable tokens unless they are included in the final output text delivered to the client. For streaming we will emit two counters: "streamed_display_tokens" (what user saw) and "streamed_aux_tokens" (non-billable telemetry).
5) Backward compatibility: expose a migration audit flag for 30 days that enables both old and new counters in the ledger for customers who request reconciliation. After that window, we keep only canonical counters.

Trade-offs:
- Latency: running an additional canonicalization step increases request tail by ~0.5-1ms in microbenchmarks. We judged this acceptable because it prevents larger customer confusion and legal risk.
- Complexity vs transparency: introducing expansion diffs increases record size but gives customers a clear way to reconcile. We cap diff size to limit storage blow-up.

Acceptance criteria / Definition of Done:
- Billing pipeline reads from single canonicalized text for token counting across all paths (request-estimator, billing-worker, streaming-serializer).
- Quota enforcement uses the canonicalized text-length estimate at enforcement time (no earlier heuristics allowed to bypass limits).
- No duplicate billing for cached prefixes (validated by e2e test harness).
- Auxiliary streaming frames do not contribute to billable output tokens unless included in final user-visible text.
- Add audit column fields original_length and expanded_length in usage export; documented in billing FAQ.
- Automation: unit tests + integration tests cover template expansion, cached prefix dedupe, and logprob streaming; e2e synthetic dataset must show <0.01% requests with delta > 10 tokens vs canonical baseline.

Implementation plan (high level steps):
1) Add canonical_text field to request context + trace propagation (PR #redwood/infra/PR-xx).
2) Modify quota-enforcer to consult canonical_text before final enforcement.
3) Change billing-worker to token-count from canonical_text; implement dedupe step for cache hits.
4) Add streaming-serializer checks to treat auxiliary frames as non-billable unless attached to final output.
5) Add audit fields to usage exports and update billing UI docs.
6) Launch migration: 2-week canary on internal tenant, 1-week external limited rollout with reconciliation window.

Telemetry & Monitoring:
- New metrics: billing.canonicalized_token_delta (histogram), billing.double_count_rate (rate), billing.streaming_aux_token_rate.
- Dashboards: per-customer delta distribution, 95/99 pct mismatch, top 20 customers by expansion volumes.
- Alert: if billing.canonicalized_token_delta_99 > 50 for >1h, page oncall billing-engineer.

Rollout and communication:
- Post design summary to Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/BIlling/Prompt+Expansion+Billing (design doc drafted).
- Customer-facing billing FAQ entry and opt-in reconciliation export for first 30 days.
- Internal announcement to Solutions/Support with example requests and instructions for reconciliation.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: audit window increases storage and query costs. Mitigation: cap expansion diff payload and drop raw diffs after 90 days.
- Risk: small latency regression. Mitigation: microbenchmark and optimize canonicalizer; revert if >5% tail increase.

Open questions / decisions needed from PM/legal:
- Do we bill customers for expansion tokens or the pre-expanded token count in any circumstance? (Recommendation: bill expanded tokens, but show both counts and provide temporary reconciliation.)
- Do enterprise contracts need an exception window? (Eng to coordinate with Sales.)

- Design doc draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/BIlling/Prompt+Expansion+Billing

comments: 2026-02-22 Miguel Torres: Ran the 50k synthetic test locally; attaching sample traces in the PR. Observed tokenizer run twice in 17% of code paths. Adding canonical_text to context looks simplest.

2026-03-02 Dan Li (Billing eng): Reviewed billing dedupe approach. Concern: comparing token spans requires stable token ids across tokenizer versions. Proposal: use normalized utf8 canonical text comparison as fallback.
